R-related to EI-20577421906951067, not a duplicate: this one is the OVER-FIRE (things get closed that should not be), that one is the IRREVERSIBILITY (a wrong closure cannot be undone). They are two halves of one trap and neither is safe to fix alone — fixing only the over-fire leaves existing bad closures stuck; fixing only the reopen path leaves the source of them running.             "terminalOwner": "su-48ed7aaf-a682-4059-b032-42e9488f6620",
            "terminalCompletionRef": "Root cause found + fixed + LIVE-VERIFIED. The hive epoch was never advancing past 0 because papercusp-hive-rekey resolved false on the rig sidecar (a stale PG flag-override shadowing the compiled DEFAULT-ON — confirmed live: /api/flags/set returned backend:'pg-override', posthogFailureReason:'flag-backend-not-configured'), so advanceEpochOnHiveBoundary silently no-op'd (applied:false, no throw, and — before this fix — no stdout signal either) on every revoke. With the epoch stuck at 0, post-ban content stayed under the same key the banned member already held: not a leak in the crypto/K-cut design, a test-rig gap that left the mechanism unarmed (same class two-instance-hive-from-repo-smoke.sh already hit and fixed for its own leg, su-9140a 2026-06-19 — the deb-hetzner-*.sh rigs never got the equivalent fix)."
          }
        ],
        "claim_hold_reason": "P2P/federation item (hive epoch K-cut revocation leak in the deb-hetzner federation gate rig) — out of scope for the non-P2P drain fleet per plan Decision D-002 (claimHold-as-fence loop).       }
